findings.title: Boot `apply` waits the full 10 s on every Intel machine whose panel can't self-refresh.
findings.body: The loop only stops early if `helper::find` returns a PSR-capable panel or no Intel display is bound. On an Intel desktop with no eDP, or on a laptop whose panel supports neither PSR nor Panel Replay, `intel_display()` is true and `find()` is always `None`. The loop then sleeps 100 × 100 ms on every boot. The unit is a `Type=oneshot` wanted by `multi-user.target`, which by default is ordered after the units it wants, so reaching multi-user.target is delayed by 10 s on all of these machines. Fix: stop waiting once the driver's debugfs directory exists, even if no `i915_edp_psr_debug` or no sink support is found. Only wait while the driver is bound and its debugfs entries have not appeared yet.

findings.title: Quick on/off toggles start pkexec helpers that run concurrently, so the kernel can end in the opposite state to the switch.
findings.body: Each flip spawns its own `pkexec aizome-panel-refresh on|off` and nothing serializes them. If the user flips on and then off quickly, the two root helpers race. Both write `panel-refresh.new` and rename it into the choice file, and both write the debugfs file, so the last one to finish wins. If `on` finishes last, PSR is on and is kept on across reboots, while `self.panel_refresh` is `Some(false)`. Both results are `Ok`, so the menu keeps showing it as off. Fix: serialize the calls. Keep one in-flight task and queue the latest wanted value, then rerun once the task finishes if that value differs. A file lock in the helper would also work.

findings.title: The boot service is not ordered after the GPU driver binds, so PSR can stay at the driver default (on).
findings.body: The unit is ordered only after `sys-kernel-debug.mount`. If it starts before udev has probed xe/i915, `intel_display()` returns false and the wait loop exits at once. `find()` then finds nothing, an unavailable status is written, and nothing goes to debugfs. The panel then runs with the driver's default (PSR/Panel Replay on) and the menu shows no switch. That contradicts "off until turned on" and can bring back the flashing and lag this PR is meant to avoid. I couldn't check how early xe loads in your initrd setup, so whether this happens depends on the machine. Fix: trigger the apply from a udev rule on the drm card's `add` event, or order the unit after the backlight or drm device unit (or `systemd-udev-settle`). Alternatively, make the helper wait while a display-class PCI device exists that has no bound driver yet.
